audit.whatIsWrong: The TL;DR (and the identical report[0].t) asserted 'Wind Wall does NOT block soldier autos'. That is backwards and it is the single most important interaction in the matchup.
audit.why: enemyKit W: 'Creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds', flagged blocksProjectiles — 'deletes enemy projectile damage entirely'. Azir's Sand Soldier attacks 'deal magic damage to enemies in a line' and are projectiles, as is the Q drag-through. Wind Wall eats both.
audit.corrected: TL;DR and report[0].t now state that Wind Wall blocks soldier attacks outright for 4 seconds on a 25-second rank-1 cooldown, and the poke advice is keyed to that downtime.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer sides read Yasuo on all seven rows while the content layer and the packet levelChart both read Yasuo/Yasuo/Yasuo/Yasuo/Azir/Azir/Azir — three rows rendering two answers, and rows 4-6 carried whys describing Azir winning under a Yasuo verdict.
audit.why: 52.55% over 1488 games is Azir-favoured overall, and Emperor's Divide is terrain that stops Sweeping Blade mid-dash while Last Breath requires an airborne target. The flip at 6 is real.
audit.corrected: phases[4..6].side moved to Azir to match win[4..6]; all seven whys rewritten with Yasuo's real numbers.

audit.why: Spike order is right: Yasuo threatens from level 3 on the Steel Tempest knockup, Azir's level 6 Emperor's Divide is the inflection, Nashor's widens it. Grounded further with the 70/50/30s Last Breath cooldown and the terrain interaction rather than replaced.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and dosFull[1].d now say WHY 6 flips it: R is terrain, and Last Breath needs an airborne target.

audit.why: It is the field that exists to hold cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall 25s/4s duration, Sweeping Blade 0.5s recast, Azir E 22s all stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim under 'Wall his EQ-knockup engage with R' and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under 'Waste the wall on a half-committed engage' (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED). dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[0].d also described something other than their titles.
audit.why: Each title promises a specific action the body never explained.
audit.corrected: Five bodies rewritten to their own titles using Yasuo's ranges, cooldowns and the terrain interaction.

audit.why: packet.suspectNames flagged spikes[1].text 'Sweeping Blade's' as a probable wrong name; Sweeping Blade is Yasuo's real E in the kit file. False positive, left alone.

edits.before: Wind Wall does NOT block soldier autos — but his dash-chain through the wave reaches you anyway; poke and PIVOT before the third dash.
edits.after: Wind Wall blocks your soldier attacks outright — 4 seconds of nothing on a 25s cooldown. Poke before he drops it, then pivot off his dash-chain.

edits.before: W a soldier behind the wave and farm THROUGH it — your auto range is the soldier's range. Don't poke yet; sand costs mana.
edits.after: Steel Tempest is 475 range on a 4s cooldown and counts as an auto. W behind the wave, farm through it, spend no mana on poke.

edits.before: Two soldiers up means a real trade: W-Q the drag-through and step back. The poke is free only when his engage is down.
edits.after: Two soldiers let you drag a Q through him, but his second Steel Tempest stack is a knockup — trade and step off the line.

edits.before: E completes the safety net — you now have the shield-dash out. Greedier soldier placements are allowed, not encouraged.
edits.after: E is your shield-dash out. Sweeping Blade recasts every 0.5s through minions, so never leave a lone soldier beside you.

edits.before: Nashor's components arrive and the soldier DPS starts to sting. Drag Qs through Yasuo on every last-hit he takes.
edits.after: Drag Qs through his last-hit steps, but Wind Wall on 21s at rank 3 deletes the poke if you telegraph it.

edits.before: Emperor's Divide online — the dive insurance and the insec flip. With R up you win every 2v2 your jungler joins.
edits.after: Emperor's Divide is terrain: it stops Sweeping Blade mid-dash and knocks him out of his own all-in. The lane flips here.

edits.before: Nashor's spike: your soldier poke becomes shred. Shove crashes and rotate — the soldiers siege towers better than any mid.
edits.after: Nashor's spike: soldier poke becomes shred. Crash waves and make him come through a wall his dash cannot cross.

edits.before: Full build Azir is a teamfight: R cuts the fight in half, soldiers melt whoever is on your side of the wall.
edits.after: Full build your wall splits him off his team, and Last Breath needs an airborne target he can no longer make.

edits.before: Yasuo wins by landing Wind Wall, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Yasuo drops Wind Wall on your soldiers, dashes in on his second Steel Tempest stack, and Last Breath holds you up for the rest.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E Shifting Sands for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1 and lasts 4 seconds: it eats soldier attacks and your Q, so hold poke until it is spent. - Sweeping Blade recasts in 0.5s but never on the same target. - Budget E Shifting Sands (22s) for emergencies.

edits.before: Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Land the soldier auto as the waves meet, then step off his 475-range dash line before he chains a second Sweeping Blade.

edits.before: W behind the wave, Q-drag the soldier through Yasuo on his last-hit, auto once through the soldier, step back — two-second trades he cannot answer without overextending.
edits.after: Emperor's Divide is terrain — it stops Sweeping Blade mid-dash, and Last Breath needs an airborne target. Wall the moment his second Steel Tempest stack lands, not after.

edits.before: Yasuo spends Wind Wall early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Q-drag the soldier across the gap he has to dash through — the slow costs him the follow-up.

edits.before: That’s Yasuo’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: His shield builds while he moves; standing still just feeds a Q3 knockup.

edits.before: Standing at max soldier range admiring your poke with E on cooldown — that is the engage window every Yasuo player is waiting for.
edits.after: R is 120 seconds at rank 1. Spend it on the dash that actually commits, not on the first Sweeping Blade poke through a minion.

edits.before: Ahead, siege: crash waves with soldier autos, take every plate, and rotate to river with R held — your wall converts even fights into massacres.
edits.after: Ahead, siege: crash with soldier autos, take plates while Wind Wall's 25 seconds is down, and rotate with R held to wall off his dash lane.

edits.before: Carry through siege control — soldiers take plates, R denies engages, and your DPS curve outlasts every assassin spike in the lobby.
edits.after: Carry through siege — soldiers take plates, and Emperor's Divide is terrain that stops the dash chain his whole damage pattern needs.

edits.before: If Yasuo takes first blood, tighten up: Wind Wall is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm at soldier range and stay relevant through wave control.
edits.after: If Yasuo takes first blood, tighten up: assume Wind Wall is up and never poke into it. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn't — farm at soldier range and hold R for his engage.

edits.before: Yasuo is genuinely dangerous pre-6 — Sweeping Blade lets him dash through any soldier or minion to close the gap instantly, and if he lands a tornado knockup he can combo you down with autos before you can react. Be careful about leaving isolated soldiers near you, and use your dash defensively rather than aggressively until you have your own ultimate to answer his engage.
edits.after: Yasuo is genuinely dangerous pre-6 — Sweeping Blade recasts every 0.5 seconds to dash through any soldier or minion, and Wind Wall deletes your soldier attacks and your Q outright for 4 seconds on a 25-second cooldown. Never leave an isolated soldier beside you, poke only once the wall is spent, and keep your dash for escaping rather than entering until your own ultimate answers his engage.

notes: The TL;DR fix is the calibration case named in the brief — the page was asserting the opposite of Riot's own Wind Wall text. Only two report[] entries were touched and report[0].t was one of them solely because it duplicated the false TL;DR string verbatim. phases[N].rating left untouched: the rating scale on this champion is not internally consistent, so blind moves risked making it worse.
